..
An unsettled weather pattern produced by an extensive monsoon trough
dominated primarily by a developing disturbance known as Invest 93W 
well to the east, is expected to continue as such the next few days.
Mostly dry conditions are expected overnight, followed by some
island showers developing Tuesday afternoon. After, conditions will
deteriorate once again as Invest 93W continues to consolidate and
pass to the northeast of the Marianas sometime Thursday through 
Friday, inducing a significant monsoon surge that will bring a peak 
in shower and thunder potential by the weekend. Conditions are then 
expected to remain wet coming into next week as a southerwesterly 
monsoon regime continues.

Marine...
Seas around 3 feet will remain overnight, to then increase thereafter
as Invest 93W continues to consolidate to the east of the Marianas 
and allowing a southwesterly monsoon to return across the region 
toward the next weekend. As 93W passes to the northeast and a monsoon
surge develops, seas are expected to surpass 10 feet beginning 
Thursday, likely becoming hazardous to small craft. A low risk of rip
currents is expected along all reefs of the Marianas through at 
least Wednesday, when a moderate rip current risk may develop along 
west facing reefs. There is some likelihood for hazardous surf to 
develop along south, west and north facing reefs of the Marianas in 
the second half of the week, highly dependent on the development of 
93W and associated southwesterly monsoon surge.

Tropical Systems...
A developing disturbance, Invest 93W, is found along the monsoon 
trough, centered well east of the Marianas, north-northeast of Weno,
Chuuk, near 15N157E. This system is rated as a sub-low. 93W has 
moved slowly west-northwest and is expected to slowly strengthen as 
it continues to move west-northwest to northwest over the next few 
days, possibly passing north of Saipan, moving through the northern 
CNMI. Residents of the Marianas, especially Tinian, Saipan and the 
northern CNMI, should monitor forecasts for any changes to expected 
development and movement over the next few days.

Eastern Micronesia...
A very dry pattern is now in place over Pohnpei and Kosrae and is
expected to continue through the remainder of the week. For Majuro,
dry conditions will continue through Tuesday night. Then, the eastern
end of the monsoon trough looks to become a bit more active as Invest
93W moves out to the west-northwest and drags the trough over the
Marshall Islands. The trough looks to make a very slow progression
toward Kosrae and Pohnpei and could possibly begin to affect both
locations over the weekend.

Fairly benign marine conditions look to continue across the region
through the week, with seas of 3 to 5 feet and light to gentle winds
at all three locations through at least Friday.

Western Micronesia...
The monsoon trough remains the dominant feature in the region. The 
trough axis is located near 10N130E and extends eastward across much
of Micronesia and ending near 10N155E. This feature is producing 
scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms, with the 
strongest showers near 10N. As Invest 93W consolidates and moves 
west- northwest, the axis is expected to turn into a more NE-SW 
direction.

Palau is south of the trough, far enough that showers will vary 
between isolated and scattered through about Thursday. During this 
time, 93W is expected to continue consolidating and moving west-
northwest direction, this will cause a shift in the trough's axis, 
allowing for more favorable conditions for showers to be produced 
over Palau for the weekend.

Yap is the closest island to this trough and expected to see
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms through the week. Model
guidance suggests up to 1 inch of rain each day through the 
remainder of the week. Overall, a wet week is to be expected.

Chuuk is on the southern edge of the convective activity produced by
the monsoon trough. Here is where blow-off cloud cover is the 
greatest. This cloud cover is expected to produce isolated showers 
while the trough remains in a E-W orientation. Once 93W starts
pulling the trough away, drier conditions are expected to return
for the weekend and into next week.

Altimetry shows combined seas between 3 and 5 feet across the 
region. Winds will be light to moderate through Thursday, then winds 
are expected to build to gentle to fresh near the weekend. Sea 
conditions are expected to remain benign through Thursday, afterwards
seas are anticipated to build to around 9 feet along the northern 
portions of the region. A Small Craft Advisory may become necessary 
for the weekend.
